value.recommendation: Focus workload design on simplicity and efficiency. Use a practical approach to avoid unnecessary complexity while meeting your business goals and requirements.
value.typical_thresholds: No universal numeric target. Principle is qualitative â€” every added component must justify its reliability cost.
value.risk_summary: Over-engineered architectures accumulate hidden failure points. Each unnecessary component is a potential outage vector and increases operational overhead.

value.recommendation: Identify and rate user and system flows. Use a criticality scale based on your business requirements to prioritise the flows.
value.typical_thresholds: Critical flows typically require higher SLOs (99.99%+) than supporting flows (99.9%). Exact targets depend on business requirements.
value.risk_summary: Without flow prioritisation, teams apply uniform reliability investment. Critical revenue paths receive the same treatment as low-value background jobs.

value.recommendation: Use failure mode analysis (FMA) to identify potential failures in your workload. Identify dependencies and failure points, and develop mitigation strategies for those failures.
value.typical_thresholds: All P0/P1 failure modes should have documented mitigation strategies. 100% mitigation coverage for critical path dependencies.
value.risk_summary: Unknown failure modes surface as production incidents. Without FMA, the blast radius of any failure is undefined and potentially unbounded.

value.recommendation: Define reliability and recovery targets for your workload. Use the targets to inform your design and as the foundation of your health model.
value.typical_thresholds: Production APIs: 99.9%â€“99.99% uptime. RTO: 1â€“4 hours non-critical, 15â€“60 min critical. RPO: 5â€“60 minutes. Error rate: < 0.1% at steady state.
value.risk_summary: Without defined RTO/RPO, teams have no agreed recovery speed. Failures become open-ended incidents with no measurable success criteria for resolution.

value.recommendation: Add redundancy at different levels, especially for critical flows. Consider redundant infrastructure components such as compute and network, and multiple instances of your solution.
value.typical_thresholds: Minimum 2 replicas for production stateless services. Multi-AZ for any service with >= 99.9% SLO. Multi-region for >= 99.99% SLO.
value.risk_summary: Single-region or single-zone deployment means one datacenter event causes total outage. Single instance deployments have no tolerance for host-level failures.

value.recommendation: Implement a timely and reliable scaling strategy at the application, data, and infrastructure levels. Base the scaling strategy on actual or predicted usage patterns.
value.typical_thresholds: Scale-out latency < 120 seconds for most App Service / AKS workloads. CPU utilisation trigger: 60â€“70% to allow headroom before saturation.
value.risk_summary: Without autoscaling, sudden demand spikes overwhelm fixed capacity. Manual scaling cannot respond fast enough to viral traffic events.

value.recommendation: Strengthen the resiliency of your workload by implementing self-preservation and self-healing measures. Use built-in features and well-established cloud patterns.
value.typical_thresholds: Retry policies: 3 attempts with exponential backoff. Circuit breaker open threshold: 50% failure rate over 30 seconds. Health check intervals: 30 seconds.
value.risk_summary: Without circuit breakers and retry policies, transient failures become sustained outages. Tight coupling between services enables cascade failure.

value.recommendation: Test for resiliency and availability scenarios by applying the principles of chaos engineering. Perform active malfunction and simulated load testing.
value.typical_thresholds: Chaos experiments: minimum quarterly for production, monthly for staging. Load tests before every major release. Recovery drill: annually minimum.
value.risk_summary: DR plans that have never been drilled will fail under pressure. Untested assumptions about system resilience are frequently wrong.

value.recommendation: Implement structured, tested, and documented disaster recovery plans that align with the recovery targets. Plans must cover all components and the system as a whole.
value.typical_thresholds: DR plan must cover 100% of components on the critical path. Drill results must meet defined RTO/RPO targets within 10% tolerance.
value.risk_summary: Undocumented DR procedures lead to confusion and extended downtime during incidents. Components with no recovery plan become single points of failure.

value.recommendation: Measure and model the solution's health signals. Continuously capture uptime and other reliability data from across the workload and from individual components and key flows.
value.typical_thresholds: MTTD < 5 minutes for P1 incidents. Health probe coverage: 100% of production services. Alert false positive rate: < 10%.
value.risk_summary: Without health monitoring, failures are discovered by users before the team. No observability means no early warning and slower incident response.

value.recommendation: Establish a security baseline aligned to compliance requirements, industry standards, and platform recommendations. Regularly measure your workload architecture and operations against the baseline.
value.typical_thresholds: Microsoft Defender for Cloud secure score: target >= 80%. Zero critical policy violations in production. Baseline review: quarterly minimum.
value.risk_summary: Without a defined baseline, there is no systematic way to identify gaps. Security posture drifts over time as new components are added without review.

value.recommendation: Maintain a secure development lifecycle with a hardened, automated, and auditable software supply chain. Incorporate threat modelling to safeguard against security-defeating implementations.
value.typical_thresholds: 100% of PRs scanned via SAST before merge. Zero known critical vulnerabilities in merged dependencies. Threat model updated on every major feature.
value.risk_summary: Without supply chain security, malicious or vulnerable dependencies reach production. Security issues missed in development are exponentially more expensive to fix later.

value.recommendation: Classify and consistently apply sensitivity and information type labels on all workload data and systems. Use classification to influence workload design and security prioritisation.
value.typical_thresholds: 100% of data stores classified. No production data stores with undefined sensitivity level.
value.risk_summary: Without classification, all data receives the same (usually insufficient) protection. High-sensitivity data may be stored or transmitted without appropriate controls.

value.recommendation: Create intentional segmentation and perimeters in your architecture design and in the workload's footprint. Include networks, roles, workload identities, and resource organisation.
value.typical_thresholds: All production data services accessible only via private endpoints. No public-IP data storage in production. Network segmentation validated via automated policy.
value.risk_summary: Flat networks allow lateral movement after initial breach. A single compromised service can access all others without segmentation.

value.recommendation: Implement strict, conditional, and auditable identity and access management across all users, team members, and system components. Limit access exclusively to as necessary.
value.typical_thresholds: 100% authentication coverage on all production API endpoints. MFA enforced for 100% of human identities. Zero standing privileged access without JIT. MTTR for critical CVEs: <= 72 hours.
value.risk_summary: Overly permissive IAM roles are exploited when accounts are compromised. Excessive privileges expand the blast radius of any breach.

value.recommendation: Isolate, filter, and control network traffic across both ingress and egress flows. Apply defence-in-depth at all available network boundaries.
value.typical_thresholds: WAF enabled on all public-facing endpoints. Egress filtered to approved destinations only. Network security group rules reviewed quarterly.
value.risk_summary: Without network controls, attackers who gain initial access can communicate freely with external C2 servers and exfiltrate data.

value.recommendation: Encrypt data using modern, industry-standard methods to guard confidentiality and integrity. Align the encryption scope with data classifications.
value.typical_thresholds: 100% of data at rest encrypted with AES-256 or platform-managed keys. 100% of data in transit using TLS 1.2 minimum (TLS 1.3 preferred). Zero HTTP endpoints in production.
value.risk_summary: Unencrypted data at rest is fully exposed in a storage breach. Unencrypted transit exposes credentials and PII to network interception.

value.recommendation: Harden all workload components by reducing extraneous surface area and tightening configurations to increase attacker cost.
value.typical_thresholds: Zero unnecessary open ports in production. CIS benchmark score >= 90% for all compute resources. Container images scanned and no critical CVEs.
value.risk_summary: Every unnecessary service or open port is an attack vector. Default configurations are well-known to attackers and frequently exploited.

value.recommendation: Protect application secrets by hardening their storage, restricting access and manipulation, auditing those actions, and running a reliable rotation process.
value.typical_thresholds: Zero hardcoded secrets in source code (enforced by secret scanning in CI). 100% of secrets stored in Key Vault or equivalent. Rotation: 90 days for API keys, 365 days for certificates.
value.risk_summary: Secrets in source code are exposed in repository history, logs, and build artefacts. Unrotated secrets remain valid after personnel changes or breaches.

value.recommendation: Implement a holistic monitoring strategy that relies on modern threat detection mechanisms integrated with the platform. Mechanisms should reliably alert for triage.
value.typical_thresholds: MTTD for critical security alerts: < 15 minutes. False positive rate < 5%. 100% of production resources onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Cloud.
value.risk_summary: Without security monitoring, breaches are discovered weeks or months after initial compromise. Insufficient logging prevents forensic investigation and root cause analysis.

value.recommendation: Establish a comprehensive testing regimen that combines approaches to prevent security issues, validate threat prevention implementations, and test threat detection mechanisms.
value.typical_thresholds: Penetration test: annually minimum, after major architectural changes. DAST on every release to staging. Critical and high vulnerabilities remediated within SLA (72h critical, 7 days high).
value.risk_summary: Security controls that have never been tested may not work. Assumed mitigations frequently fail when validated against realistic attack scenarios.

value.recommendation: Define and test effective incident response procedures covering a spectrum of incidents, from localised issues to disaster recovery. Clearly assign ownership.
value.typical_thresholds: IR plan covers 100% of identified threat scenarios. Security MTTR (mean time to contain): <= 4 hours for critical incidents. IR drill: minimum annually.
value.risk_summary: Without tested incident response, security incidents become prolonged, chaotic, and more damaging. Unclear ownership leads to coordination failure during high-pressure events.

value.recommendation: Create a culture of financial responsibility. Regularly train personnel, foster creativity and spending accountability, and invest in tooling and automation.
value.typical_thresholds: All engineers with Azure access complete cost awareness training annually. Cost anomaly alerts configured on all subscriptions.
value.risk_summary: Without financial accountability, individual engineers make expensive infrastructure choices without visibility into cost impact. Spend grows unchecked.

value.recommendation: Create and maintain a cost model. A cost model should estimate the initial cost, run rates, and ongoing costs. Negotiate a budget with a buffer for unplanned spending.
value.typical_thresholds: Budget variance: < 10% month-over-month. Forecast accuracy within 15% of actuals. Budget buffer: 15â€“20% above expected run rate.
value.risk_summary: Without a cost model, there is no baseline to detect overspend. Actual costs routinely exceed estimates by 2â€“5x when not modelled upfront.

value.recommendation: Collect and review cost data daily. Capture incurred costs, prepaid costs, trends, and forecasts. Automate alerts at key thresholds and detect anomalies.
value.typical_thresholds: Budget alert at 80% consumed. Anomaly alert for daily spend > 20% above 7-day average. Cost per 1k API requests tracked as primary efficiency metric.
value.risk_summary: Without daily cost visibility, overruns are discovered at month-end when it is too late to correct. Egress charges and idle resources accumulate silently.

value.recommendation: Set spending guardrails including release gates, governance policies, resource limits, and access controls. Prioritise platform automation over manual processes.
value.typical_thresholds: Zero unapproved resource types in production. Azure Policy deny effects for non-approved SKUs. Resource group budget limits enforced.
value.risk_summary: Without guardrails, developers provision expensive resources (GPU VMs, large databases) that are forgotten and run indefinitely.

value.recommendation: Get the best rates from providers. Find and use the best rates for cloud resources and licenses. Review cost savings including reserved instances and commitment plans.
value.typical_thresholds: Reserved instance coverage: >= 70% of stable baseline compute. Savings plan utilisation: >= 90% of commitment. Review pricing tiers quarterly.
value.risk_summary: Pay-as-you-go pricing for stable baseline workloads is 30â€“60% more expensive than reserved capacity. Significant ongoing waste without optimised billing.

value.recommendation: Align usage to billing increments. Understand billing meters and modify resource usage or service configuration to align with billing increments.
value.typical_thresholds: Qualitative. Audit billing meters for top 5 cost drivers and validate usage patterns match billing increments. Review after architecture changes.
value.risk_summary: Misaligned usage can cause disproportionate billing. A workload that runs for 61 minutes in an hourly-billed service pays for 2 hours.

value.recommendation: Optimise component costs. Regularly remove or optimise legacy, unneeded, and underutilised workload components, application features, and platform resources.
value.typical_thresholds: CPU average utilisation: review resources below 20% for downsizing. Zero idle resources (0 requests in 30 days) in production. Monthly resource audit.
value.risk_summary: Over-provisioned VMs and App Service plans pay for capacity that is never used. Orphaned resources (unused disks, old snapshots) accumulate ongoing charges.

value.recommendation: Optimise environment costs. Align spending to prioritise production, preproduction, and DR environments. Non-production environments should emulate but not replicate production costs.
value.typical_thresholds: Non-production cost: typically 10â€“30% of production. Dev/test environments shut down outside business hours (target: <= 40% uptime vs production 99%+).
value.risk_summary: Dev/test environments running 24/7 at production scale account for a disproportionate share of total spend. Common source of 30â€“50% cost savings when addressed.

value.recommendation: Optimise flow costs. Align the cost of each flow with flow priority. Consider features, functionality, and nonfunctional requirements of each flow.
value.typical_thresholds: Cost per critical user flow tracked as primary unit metric. Non-critical flows should cost < 50% of equivalent critical flow where architecturally feasible.
value.risk_summary: Uniform cost treatment across flows means low-value flows consume resources that should be reserved for revenue-critical paths.

value.recommendation: Optimise data costs. Improve data management including tiering and retention, volume, replication, backups, file formats, and storage solutions.
value.typical_thresholds: Data egress: monitored and budgeted. Blob storage: hot/cool/archive tiering applied based on access frequency. Backup retention: matches RPO, not maximum available.
value.risk_summary: Unmonitored data egress charges are consistently underestimated. Storing all data in hot tier when most is archival wastes 60â€“80% of storage cost.

value.recommendation: Optimise code costs. Evaluate and modify code to meet functional and nonfunctional requirements with fewer or cheaper resources.
value.typical_thresholds: Serverless functions: target execution time reduction of >= 20% per optimisation cycle. Memory allocation: review functions/containers using < 50% allocated memory.
value.risk_summary: Inefficient code consumes excessive compute. A function with unnecessary DB calls or blocking I/O can cost 10x more than an optimised equivalent.

value.recommendation: Optimise scaling costs. Evaluate alternative scaling configurations and align with the cost model. Use strategies for controlling demand and supply.
value.typical_thresholds: Autoscale scale-in must be configured alongside scale-out. Review peak vs average instance count ratio â€” a ratio > 3x suggests demand shaping opportunity.
value.risk_summary: Scaling only upward without scale-in leads to over-provisioned baseline after traffic peaks. Capped scaling limits may cause reliability failures at unexpected demand.

value.recommendation: Optimise personnel time. Align the time personnel spends on tasks with the priority of the task. Minimise noise, reduce build times, and enable high-fidelity debugging.
value.typical_thresholds: CI build time: target < 10 minutes for standard PR builds. Alert noise ratio (actionable vs total): target > 80% actionable. On-call page frequency: < 5 P1/P2 per engineer per month.
value.risk_summary: Excessive alert noise causes alert fatigue and missed genuine incidents. Long build times slow delivery cycles and increase cost of development.

value.recommendation: Consolidate resources and responsibility. Look for consolidation opportunities within the workload and use existing centralised resources where appropriate.
value.typical_thresholds: Identify and eliminate duplicate services performing identical functions. Centralised observability (Log Analytics workspace) shared across workloads where feasible.
value.risk_summary: Redundant services performing the same function multiply cost without adding reliability. Multiple separate Log Analytics workspaces are a common source of avoidable spend.

value.recommendation: Define standard practices to develop and operate your workload. Align team specialisations with clear practices for designing, deploying, and operating the workload.
value.typical_thresholds: 100% of operational processes documented. Runbooks reviewed and updated quarterly. Onboarding time for new engineers <= 2 weeks to productive contribution.
value.risk_summary: Undocumented practices create key-person dependency. Knowledge leaves when people leave. Inconsistent practices lead to inconsistent outcomes.

value.recommendation: Use standardisation to make routine, ad-hoc, and emergency operations consistent and predictable. Codify runbooks and standard operating procedures.
value.typical_thresholds: Runbooks for all P1/P2 incident types. Manual steps in critical operations: target zero, max 3. SOP review cycle: quarterly.
value.risk_summary: Ad-hoc emergency operations performed differently each time produce inconsistent outcomes and extend incident duration.

value.recommendation: Formalise processes across the full software development lifecycle, from ideation to delivery, and make them transparent to the team and stakeholders.
value.typical_thresholds: Cycle time (commit to production): target < 1 day for small changes. Lead time: measured and trending down sprint-over-sprint. Process compliance: >= 95%.
value.risk_summary: Informal development processes accumulate technical debt and make quality unpredictable. Stakeholders cannot track progress without formalised workflow.

value.recommendation: Enhance software development and quality assurance using industry-standard practices. Standardise tools, source control, design patterns, documentation, and style guides.
value.typical_thresholds: Code review: 100% of PRs reviewed before merge. Unit test coverage: >= 80% for new code. Defect escape rate (bugs found in production vs pre-production): target < 10%.
value.risk_summary: Without standardised tooling and practices, code quality is inconsistent and defects escape to production at higher rates.

value.recommendation: Use a standardised infrastructure as code approach to prepare resources and configurations. Prefer declarative over imperative approaches when practical.
value.typical_thresholds: IaC coverage: 100% of production infrastructure defined in code. Zero manual changes to production resources outside IaC pipeline. Drift detection: automated, daily.
value.risk_summary: Manual infrastructure changes are not repeatable, not auditable, and cannot be rolled back reliably. Configuration drift between environments causes dev/prod parity failures.

value.recommendation: Build a workload supply chain that drives changes through predictable, automated pipelines. Test and promote changes across all environments and quality gates.
value.typical_thresholds: Deployment frequency: >= weekly for production. Pipeline success rate: >= 95%. Change failure rate: < 5%. All production deployments via automated pipeline.
value.risk_summary: Manual deployments are inconsistent and error-prone. Without quality gates, breaking changes reach production without detection.

value.recommendation: Design and implement a monitoring system to capture and expose telemetry, metrics, and logs from your infrastructure and code. Use data to validate design choices.
value.typical_thresholds: 100% of production services emitting structured telemetry. Log ingestion latency: < 60 seconds for real-time alerting. All P1 flows covered by dashboards.
value.risk_summary: Without centralised logging and distributed tracing, diagnosing issues across service boundaries is impossible. Incidents are longer and more impactful.

value.recommendation: Establish a clear, structured incident management process with defined roles, documented procedures, and architecture designed for rapid detection, diagnosis, and recovery.
value.typical_thresholds: MTTD: < 5 minutes for P1. MTTR: < 30 minutes for P1, < 4 hours for P2. Incident recurrence rate (same root cause): < 10%. Post-incident review within 48 hours.
value.risk_summary: Without defined incident management, response is chaotic and extended. The same incidents recur because root causes are never systematically addressed.

value.recommendation: Automate tasks that are repetitive, procedural, and provide a clear return on investment. Prefer off-the-shelf automation over custom solutions.
value.typical_thresholds: All routine operational tasks (backups, patching, certificate rotation) automated. Manual operational time: trending down quarter-over-quarter.
value.risk_summary: Manual repetitive tasks introduce human error, are not scalable, and consume engineering time that could be spent on higher-value work.

value.recommendation: Design and implement automation upfront for tasks like lifecycle management, bootstrapping, and governance. Avoid retrofitting automation later.
value.typical_thresholds: Resource lifecycle policies (retention, cleanup) defined for 100% of resource types at creation. Bootstrap automation tested on every deploy.
value.risk_summary: Retrofitting automation into an already-running system is significantly harder and more risky than building it in from the start.

value.recommendation: Clearly define your workload's safe deployment practices. Focus on small, incremental releases with quality gates. Use modern deployment patterns and progressive exposure.
value.typical_thresholds: Deployment success rate: >= 95%. Change failure rate: < 5%. Rollback time: < 15 minutes. Canary deployments: start at 5â€“10% traffic before full rollout.
value.risk_summary: Big-bang releases accumulate risk. Without progressive exposure, a breaking change reaches 100% of users before it can be detected and rolled back.

value.recommendation: Define performance targets. Performance targets should be numerical values tied to workload requirements, implemented for all workload flows.
value.typical_thresholds: API endpoints: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 500ms at expected peak load. Throughput: validated against expected RPS at peak. Targets defined per flow, not globally.
value.risk_summary: Without defined performance targets, teams have no criteria for success. Optimisation efforts are unfocused and regressions go undetected.

value.recommendation: Conduct capacity planning before predicted changes in usage patterns such as seasonal variations, product updates, marketing campaigns, or regulatory changes.
value.typical_thresholds: Capacity headroom: >= 30% above expected peak before known events. Capacity review: 4 weeks before planned traffic events. Load forecast accuracy: within 25%.
value.risk_summary: Without capacity planning, sudden traffic spikes (marketing campaigns, viral events) overwhelm under-provisioned systems. Reactive scaling is too slow.

value.recommendation: Select the right services. Infrastructure and tier selections must support your ability to reach the workload's performance targets and accommodate expected capacity changes.
value.typical_thresholds: SKU utilisation: 40â€“70% at expected peak (headroom for spikes). Service tier review: at every major architectural change and annually.
value.risk_summary: Wrong service tier selection means either over-spend on unused capacity or performance failures at load. Tier changes often require downtime.

value.recommendation: Collect performance data. Workload components and flows should provide automatic, continuous, and meaningful metrics and logs at all levels.
value.typical_thresholds: 100% of production services emitting performance metrics. Trace sampling: >= 10% for normal traffic, 100% during load tests. Metrics retention: >= 30 days.
value.risk_summary: Without performance data, regressions go undetected until they affect users. Profiling without baselines cannot identify what has changed.

value.recommendation: Optimise scaling and partitioning. Incorporate reliable and controlled scaling and partitioning. Base the scale unit design on the workload's scaling strategy.
value.typical_thresholds: No partition hotspots (single partition handling > 3x average load). Scale-out triggered before saturation (< 80% utilisation threshold). Scale unit tested at 2x expected peak.
value.risk_summary: Poor partitioning creates hotspots that cannot be resolved by scaling. Scaling units that are too coarse waste resource; too fine creates coordination overhead.

value.recommendation: Test performance regularly in an environment that matches the production environment. Compare results against the performance targets and the performance benchmark.
value.typical_thresholds: Load testing: before every major release and monthly on stable codebases. SLO breach rate in load tests: 0%. Performance regression (> 10% degradation vs baseline) blocks release.
value.risk_summary: Performance issues discovered by real users under production load are significantly more expensive to fix than those caught in pre-production testing.

value.recommendation: Optimise code and infrastructure. Use performant code that offloads responsibilities to the platform. Use code and infrastructure only for their core purpose.
value.typical_thresholds: Hot path profiling: top 5 functions by CPU accounted for and optimised. N+1 query patterns: zero in production. Async I/O: used for all external calls.
value.risk_summary: Synchronous calls to slow downstream services block entire request threads. Database queries without indexes on hot paths cause latency spikes that scale linearly with data.

value.recommendation: Optimise data usage. Optimise data stores, partitions, and indexes for their intended and actual use in the workload.
value.typical_thresholds: Query execution time on hot paths: p95 < 20ms. Index hit rate: >= 95%. Database CPU: < 70% at expected peak load. Slow query log: reviewed weekly.
value.risk_summary: Unindexed queries on hot paths cause latency spikes that scale linearly with data volume. A missing index can turn a 5ms query into a 5s full table scan.

value.recommendation: Prioritise the performance of critical flows. Allocate workload resources and optimisation efforts to the flows that support the most important business processes.
value.typical_thresholds: Critical flows: p95 performance targets tighter than non-critical (e.g. critical: p95 <= 100ms vs non-critical: p95 <= 500ms). Critical flows monitored with dedicated alerts.
value.risk_summary: Uniform performance investment across flows means critical revenue paths compete for resources with background processes.

value.recommendation: Optimise operational tasks. Monitor and minimise the effects of software development lifecycle operations on workload performance.
value.typical_thresholds: Backup/reindex operations: scheduled outside peak hours. Operational task CPU impact: < 10% above baseline. Deployment impact on p99: < 20% increase during rollout.
value.risk_summary: Backup jobs, index rebuilds, and certificate rotations running during peak hours can degrade performance significantly and unpredictably.

value.recommendation: Respond to live performance issues. Plan how to address performance problems with clear communication lines and responsibilities. Use incidents to drive preventive measures.
value.typical_thresholds: Performance degradation MTTD: < 5 minutes (via automated alerting). MTTR for performance incidents: < 30 minutes. Post-incident preventive action tracked to completion.
value.risk_summary: Unplanned responses to performance incidents are slower and less effective. Without post-incident learning, the same performance problems recur.

value.recommendation: Continuously optimise performance. Focus on components showing deteriorating performance over time, such as databases and networking features.
value.typical_thresholds: Performance baseline reviewed monthly. Any metric showing > 10% degradation trend over 4 weeks triggers investigation. Index fragmentation: rebuild when > 30%.
value.risk_summary: Databases and caches degrade silently over time as data grows and query plans change. Without continuous monitoring, deterioration is only noticed when it becomes a user-facing issue.

value.recommendation: Ensure the product provides functions that meet stated and implied needs under specified conditions. All required functions must be present, correct, and appropriate for the intended use.
value.typical_thresholds: Requirements coverage: 100% of must-have FRs implemented and tested. Defect escape rate to production: < 1% of released stories. Functional correctness: zero P0 functional defects in release.
value.risk_summary: Incomplete or incorrect functionality directly undermines user trust and product value. Gaps between specified and implemented behaviour cause downstream integration failures and regulatory non-compliance.

value.recommendation: Design the system to perform specified functions under stated conditions for a defined period without failure. Address maturity, availability, fault tolerance, and recoverability systematically.
value.typical_thresholds: Availability: >= 99.9% for standard systems, >= 99.99% for mission-critical. MTBF: >= 720 hours for production services. MTTR: <= 30 minutes for P1 incidents. Fault tolerance: system must degrade gracefully under partial failures.
value.risk_summary: Unreliable software erodes user confidence and causes financial loss. Failures in safety-critical domains can endanger lives. Without recoverability targets, incidents have no measurable resolution criteria.

value.recommendation: Optimise resource usage relative to the amount of resources used under stated conditions. Consider time behaviour, resource utilisation, and capacity to handle anticipated load.
value.typical_thresholds: API p95 response time: <= 200ms under normal load. p99: <= 500ms. Throughput: system must sustain peak load with < 5% degradation. CPU and memory utilisation: <= 70% at peak to maintain headroom.
value.risk_summary: Poor performance efficiency causes poor user experience, increased infrastructure costs, and capacity failures under load. Unmonitored resource utilisation leads to unexpected service degradation or outages.

value.recommendation: Ensure the product can be used by specified users to achieve goals with effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction in a specified context of use. Address learnability, operability, and user error protection.
value.typical_thresholds: Task completion rate: >= 90% for primary user flows. User error rate: <= 5% on critical tasks. User satisfaction (SUS): >= 68 (industry average). WCAG 2.1 AA compliance: 100% for public-facing interfaces.
value.risk_summary: Poor usability increases support costs, causes user errors that may have downstream consequences, and reduces adoption. In regulated domains, accessibility failures result in legal liability.

value.recommendation: Protect information and data so that persons or systems have authorised access appropriate to their types and levels. Address confidentiality, integrity, non-repudiation, accountability, and authenticity.
value.typical_thresholds: 100% of API endpoints must enforce authentication. Zero critical or high CVEs unpatched beyond 72 hours. 100% of sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit. Audit log coverage: 100% of privileged actions.
value.risk_summary: Security breaches result in data loss, regulatory fines, reputational damage, and in critical infrastructure, physical harm. Without non-repudiation and accountability controls, forensic investigation after incidents is impossible.

value.recommendation: Ensure the product can exchange information with other products, systems, or components, and perform its required functions while sharing an environment and resources. Address co-existence and interoperability.
value.typical_thresholds: Integration test pass rate: 100% before release. Zero breaking API changes without a versioning policy. API contract violations in production: zero. Backward compatibility maintained for >= 2 major versions.
value.risk_summary: Incompatible systems create integration failures that break consumer applications. Breaking changes without versioning force emergency updates across dependent services and can cause production outages.

value.recommendation: Ensure the product can be effectively and efficiently modified by designated maintainers. Address modularity, reusability, analysability, modifiability, and testability.
value.typical_thresholds: Unit test coverage: >= 80% for production code paths. Cyclomatic complexity: <= 10 per function. Code duplication: <= 5%. Technical debt ratio (SonarQube): <= 5%. Mean time to implement a small change: <= 1 working day.
value.risk_summary: Poorly maintainable code increases change lead time, magnifies the cost of every bug fix and feature, and creates knowledge silos. High complexity increases defect rates and makes refactoring risky.

value.recommendation: Ensure the product can be transferred from one hardware, software, or environmental context to another with defined effectiveness and efficiency. Address adaptability, installability, and replaceability.
value.typical_thresholds: Deployment success rate across target environments: >= 99%. Zero environment-specific defects in staging that do not reproduce in production. Containerisation: 100% of services deployable from a single image. Config via environment variables: no hard-coded environment specifics.
value.risk_summary: Poor portability creates environment-specific bugs that are expensive to diagnose and fix. Lock-in to a single vendor or runtime reduces negotiating power and increases migration cost significantly.

value.recommendation: Develop an organisational understanding of cybersecurity risk to systems, people, assets, data, and capabilities. Establish an asset inventory, risk register, and governance policy that form the foundation for all other CSF functions.
value.typical_thresholds: Asset inventory coverage: >= 95% of known production assets catalogued. Risk register: 100% of critical systems with assessed risk ratings. Data classification: 100% of data stores labelled. Third-party risk assessments: 100% of critical vendors assessed annually.
value.risk_summary: Without visibility into assets and risks, teams cannot prioritise protective controls. Unknown assets become shadow IT attack vectors. Unassessed third-party risks propagate supply chain breaches.

value.recommendation: Implement appropriate safeguards to ensure delivery of critical services. Controls span identity management, access control, awareness training, data security, information protection processes, and maintenance of protective technology.
value.typical_thresholds: MFA enforcement: 100% of human identities. Patch compliance (critical): 100% within 72 hours, high: within 7 days. Security awareness training: 100% of staff annually. Data at rest encryption: 100% of sensitive data. Privileged access reviews: at least quarterly.
value.risk_summary: Weak protective controls are the primary entry point for attackers. Unpatched systems and weak authentication account for the majority of breach initial access vectors. Insider threats exploit excessive access without regular access reviews.

value.recommendation: Develop and implement appropriate activities to identify the occurrence of a cybersecurity event in a timely manner. Maintain continuous monitoring, anomaly detection, and detection process testing.
value.typical_thresholds: MTTD for critical events: <= 15 minutes. Alert coverage: 100% of critical asset categories. False positive rate: <= 10% to prevent alert fatigue. Log retention: >= 365 days for security logs. SIEM ingestion: 100% of production systems.
value.risk_summary: Slow or absent detection allows attackers to dwell undetected, increasing breach scope and cost. The average breach dwell time without effective detection exceeds 200 days. Alert fatigue from high false positives causes real threats to be missed.

value.recommendation: Develop and implement appropriate activities to take action regarding a detected cybersecurity incident. Establish response planning, communications, analysis, mitigation, and improvement processes.
value.typical_thresholds: MTTR for critical incidents: <= 4 hours. Incident response plan: covers 100% of threat scenarios in risk register. Tabletop exercises: >= 2 per year. Containment: <= 1 hour for P1 incidents. Regulatory notification (e.g. GDPR 72-hour rule): <= 72 hours from breach discovery.
value.risk_summary: Uncoordinated incident response extends breach duration and magnifies damage. Failure to notify regulators within required windows (GDPR 72 hours, HIPAA 60 days) incurs statutory penalties. Inadequate communication causes reputational damage beyond technical scope.

value.recommendation: Develop and implement appropriate activities to maintain plans for resilience and restore capabilities or services impaired due to a cybersecurity incident. Ensure recovery planning, improvements, and communications are in place.
value.typical_thresholds: RTO: <= 4 hours for critical systems, <= 24 hours for non-critical. RPO: <= 1 hour for critical systems. Recovery drills: >= 1 per year for each critical system. System restoration success rate: >= 95% in drills. Post-incident actions: 100% of P1 lessons-learned items closed within 30 days.
value.risk_summary: Untested recovery procedures fail under pressure. Organisations without tested RTO/RPO targets routinely exceed them in actual incidents. Poor post-incident improvement cycles result in repeat incidents of the same type.

value.recommendation: Measure and track the time taken to service a request. Distinguish between the latency of successful requests and the latency of failed requests, since failed requests often return fast (but misleadingly). Use percentile distributions rather than averages to capture tail latency.
value.typical_thresholds: Internal services: p99 latency <= 100ms. User-facing services: p99 <= 300ms, p999 <= 1000ms. Failed requests must not be excluded from latency histograms â€” they should be tracked in a separate series. Alert threshold typically set at 2x normal p99 baseline.
value.risk_summary: High tail latency causes timeouts in dependent services and cascading slowdowns across the call graph. Averages hide tail latency spikes that affect a significant fraction of users. Failed requests with deceptively low latency mask unhealthy service states.

value.recommendation: Measure how much demand is being placed on your system. For web services this is typically requests per second, for audio/video systems it is network I/O rate, for storage systems it is transactions or reads/writes per second.
value.typical_thresholds: System must be sized to handle peak traffic at no more than 60% of rated capacity to maintain latency headroom. Auto-scaling triggers should fire before 70% sustained utilisation. Queue depth: alert when exceeding 2x normal baseline for > 5 minutes.
value.risk_summary: Without traffic measurement, capacity planning is guesswork. Unexpected traffic spikes saturate resources before autoscaling can respond. Unchecked queue growth indicates a systemic throughput deficit that will eventually cause data loss or timeout storms.

value.recommendation: Track the rate of requests that fail, either explicitly (HTTP 5xx), implicitly (HTTP 200 with wrong content), or by policy (any response taking longer than a defined timeout SLO). Make errors a first-class metric distinct from latency.
value.typical_thresholds: Error rate for user-facing services: < 0.1% of all requests. HTTP 5xx rate: < 0.1%. Policy violations (too-slow responses counted as errors): defined by SLO. Error budget burn rate: alert at 2% burn in 1 hour or 5% burn in 6 hours (Google SRE standard).
value.risk_summary: Untracked implicit errors (correct HTTP code, wrong content) are invisible to users but violate contracts. High error rates during traffic spikes indicate capacity or dependency issues. Error budget burn alerts are the primary signal for halting risky deployments.

value.recommendation: Measure how 'full' your service is. Focus on constrained resources (CPU, memory, I/O, network bandwidth, thread pools). Saturation must be measured prospectively â€” predict when the service will hit a ceiling and act before it does.
value.typical_thresholds: CPU: alert at >= 80% sustained for 5 minutes. Memory: alert at >= 85%. Thread/connection pool: alert at >= 75% utilisation. Disk I/O: alert at >= 80% sustained. Network: alert at >= 70% of provisioned bandwidth. Services should scale out before any resource reaches 80%.
value.risk_summary: Saturated resources cause latency increases before they cause outright failures, masking the root cause. Memory saturation triggers OOM kills and cascading restarts. Thread pool saturation causes request queuing and cascading timeouts across dependent services.

value.recommendation: Define precise, measurable SLOs for each user-facing service. An SLO specifies the target value or range for a Service Level Indicator (SLI) that must be met over a rolling window. SLOs form the basis of reliability decisions, on-call escalation, and error budget management.
value.typical_thresholds: SLO attainment: the SLO itself defines the threshold (e.g. 99.9% availability over 30 days). SLI coverage: 100% of user-facing services must have defined SLIs and SLOs. SLO review: at minimum quarterly or after any SLO breach. New services must have SLOs defined before production launch.
value.risk_summary: Without SLOs, reliability is unmeasurable and reliability work cannot be prioritised. Teams default to 100% availability aspirations which are unachievable and leave no room for velocity. Absent SLOs make it impossible to determine when to halt deployments or declare incidents.

value.recommendation: Quantify the acceptable amount of unreliability (the error budget) as 1 minus the SLO target. Use the error budget to balance release velocity against reliability: when the budget is healthy, ship; when it is exhausted, freeze risky changes and focus on reliability work.
value.typical_thresholds: Error budget burn rate alert: fast burn (2% budget consumed in 1 hour) or slow burn (5% consumed in 6 hours) triggers page. Deployment freeze: when error budget is <= 0% remaining for the rolling window. Reliability investment: when error budget is exhausted, >= 50% of sprint capacity must go to reliability work.
value.risk_summary: Without error budgets, velocity-reliability tension is resolved by politics rather than data. Teams that routinely exhaust error budgets without consequence develop a culture where reliability is secondary. Error budget burn is the earliest quantitative signal that a release is degrading production.
